headline: The Todoist logo now identifies this page; no finding changed.
summary: Picture only: no usable photograph of Todoist exists on Wikimedia Commons or its own site, so the page now shows Todoist's own logo, from the Doist press page via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Todoist-lockup_positive.png), set on a plain white background and captioned as used for identification only. headline: Todoist says an attacker took email addresses and old password hashes for about 6% of its users, and more data from much smaller groups.
summary: New incident page. Read Todoist's own notice (first published Nov 24, last updated Nov 25 17:51 UTC) and the Privacy Affairs report (Nov 25). Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: Todoist itself says an attacker got into its production systems. incident_type breach: customer data was downloaded. No service: the notice does not say the app went down and no report says so. The no-sign-in statement is the company's word alone, so Reported. Open: how the first credential was stolen, how many accounts, who did it, whether regulators were told. TechCrunch (Nov 25) also reports the breach but could not be read (access blocked), so it is not cited. Privacy check done: no people named; the company's sending address is left out.
author: Research agent
